content:
“Late Night” host Seth Meyers seemed baffled by Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin’s explanation for the numerous online system outages this month – and he’s likely not the only one.

The U.S. has experienced a nationwide FAA ground stop and widespread outages at major organizations, including banks, tech companies and even the NSA. In response, Mullin gave a rambling, incoherent explanation about how they may have been caused by AI, or “SI” as the Trump administration has come to call it:

“I started talking to the tech industry, and one guy that’s very smart with tech, he asked not to mention his name. I said, ‘What could be causing all these separate outages?’ And he says, ‘I believe that it’s the SI.’ He said, because these programs aren’t designed to work as fast as SI is. And so when they contribute, or when they, um, put in a program that’s able to write codes and it goes in, it self-fixes itself. As it starts self-fixing itself, it’s like doing a change order on a house. When you change one thing in a house, everything else starts changing. That’s a ripple effect. And it causes these systems to be overranned that weren’t designed to run as fast as the SI technology is today. That was a conversation I had today. That kind of makes sense to me.”

“Does it?” Meyers asked. “Cause it makes no fucking sense to me. Sounds like a gym teacher subbing in for health class. ‘Okay, team, listen up. When the egg comes down and self-fixes itself with the sperm, it’s... think of it like a running back carrying the ball through the gap. And you know, there’s a ripple effect.’”
